title: The Breath of Life in His Hands

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Every living thing that moved on land perished - birds, livestock, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all mankind. Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died. - Gen 7:22-23a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a solemn verse, and we should not hurry past it. It speaks of "the breath of life in its nostrils" - a haunting echo of creation, when God breathed into man "the breath of life" and he became a living being (Gen 2:7). The same breath that God once gave was now withdrawn. Every creature depended, moment by moment, on the life-breath God supplies. When it was taken, all perished.

Here is a truth we easily forget: our very breath belongs to God. We did not give ourselves life, and we cannot keep ourselves alive by our own power. Every breath we take is a gift from the God "in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind" (Job 12:10). Life is fragile, held moment by moment in the hands of God.

This is humbling. We plan and build and strive as though life were ours to command, but it is a gift, dependent on God for its every moment. As Scripture says, our life "is a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes" (Jas 4:14).

Yet this same truth is deeply comforting for those who trust God. The breath in your lungs right now is His gift to you, a sign that He is sustaining you this very moment. And the One who gives physical breath offers something greater still - eternal life through Jesus, who said, "whoever lives by believing in me will never die" (John 11:26). Receive each breath as a gift, and receive the eternal life He offers.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you receive each breath as a gift from God's hand?
- Have you received the eternal life that God offers through Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, every breath I take is Your gift, and my life is held in Your hands. Teach me to live humbly and gratefully, depending on You. Thank You for the eternal life You offer in Jesus, which death cannot take away.
